research_notes: Initial research 2026-10-01: frozen/current parliamentary material, 2001 Assembly handbook, first Senate speech, first-person supermarket post, 2012 interview, Women’s Register, employer/successor histories, 2018 Hansard, indexed FOI and RSPCA annual reports, and 2018–19 reporting inspected.

No zero public/private experience inferred. Unidentified supermarket and childcare jobs may contribute once employer control, boundaries and hours are established. Woden community work, union work and Calvary charitable work remain distinct categories.

Frozen community worker 1993–98 is an aggregate, not another counted job. Named People First 1994–97 and 1988 childcare precede/overlap it. Bereavement and parental leave affect continuity but no unpaid break dates are invented. ANU 1990 versus 1991 conflict retained.

Calvary role fills a material inter-parliamentary gap. Government meetings and public hospital work do not make its church-controlled employer government-controlled. Verify legal contracting entity, self-employment versus payroll, exact end, hours and any other clients.

Follow up supermarket identity; 1988 childcare employer; Woden/People First annual reports and historical governance; all hours and leave; CPSU desk-to-organiser transition; Calvary contract and RSPCA tenure/pay; December 2014–March 2015 gap and concurrent business roles.

Source gaps: direct APH restricted, ACT FOI PDF Internal Error, RSPCA annual PDFs 403 Forbidden. Search-index snippets explicitly labelled; no inaccessible full report claimed read. Calvary historical governance and accessible Hansard supplied alternative primary evidence. No private-profile access or outreach.
